entries.not_relevant_because: The one manuscript, 'Beyond the Square-Root Exponent for Depth-Three Boolean Circuits', proves that a single language decidable in deterministic polynomial time has n-bit membership functions needing more than 2^(A√n) gates in depth-three OR–AND–OR circuits for every A > 0, at all sufficiently large n. This is circuit-complexity progress of the kind sometimes cited in the P versus NP programme, but it separates no complexity classes: the language lies in P, and the text never mentions NP or any problem in NP, so it does not decide or bear on whether P = NP.
